description:
One-click USB flasher for Vault Node images

Vault Flasher downloads the official Vault Node image, verifies its SHA-256 against the release's published digest, and writes it to a removable USB drive with a single click — with a read-back verification pass and optional WiFi presetting. It only ever offers removable USB drives (never an internal or system disk) and re-validates the target inside its elevated writer.
# Vault Manager v1.0.0

Vault Manager 1.0 is the first full release. It sets up, claims and manages your own Vault node, on a spare PC, a mini PC or a Synology NAS, and it lets you share what that node stores with your apps and your family.

## Set up a Synology NAS as a node

A new guided **Set up a server or NAS → Synology** flow.

• **Set it up for me:** enter your NAS address and DSM login, and Vault Manager does every DSM step itself. It creates the folder, uploads and checks the node image, creates and starts the Container Manager project, and reads the claim code. Your DSM password is used for that one setup and never stored. Two-factor sign-in is supported.
• **I'll do it myself:** a click-by-click guide for DSM 7.2 and 7.4, with every field and value spelled out. If your NAS has no `docker` shared folder, the guide covers that too.
• The offered node image always follows the current release, and it's checked against its published SHA-256 before use.

Tested from a clean DSM 7.2 and 7.4.1 install, with and without an existing `docker` share, end to end：node running, claimed and serving.

## Manage your node from anywhere

• Manage a node from off your home network. Vault Manager falls back to your node's secure tunnel when it can't reach it directly.
• Your owner credentials are sealed at rest in the Windows keychain (AES-256-GCM), including backups.
• The node list shows friendly app names, clear "recovering" states while a node restarts, and no more endless "checking…".
• Storage：mirror a data disk onto a spare twin, see mirror status and last-checked times, and use one clear reconfigure button.
• New **Shutdown** control, alongside Reboot.

## Spaces, invites and recovery

• Invite someone to a space as an **Editor** or a **Viewer**.
• Invite one of your apps, such as VaultDocs or VaultDrive, into a space your node stores.
• Invite links come with a QR code that is drawn locally and sized to scan reliably on a phone, even for long invites.
• **Self-service space recovery:** recover a space whose key was lost, straight from Vault Manager.
• **Rebuild in VaultDrive:** hand a damaged space off for a fast rebuild.
• Removing an app from a node, or revoking a device, can require a second owner device to confirm.

## Add-ons

Vault Manager can install signed add-ons, which run in a sandboxed frame with only the access they declare. The first is **Leaderboard Admin**, for moderating game leaderboards hosted on your node.

## Upgrading

Install over any earlier version. Your nodes, claims and settings carry over. The download names `VaultManager-x64-setup.exe` and `VaultManager-x64.msi` are unchanged, and `VaultFlasher-*` copies are included for older links.
